summary: Paul Kingsbury worked in linguistics and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under the supervision of George Cardona, completing his studies by 2002.

Paul L. Swanson is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Otani University and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD ~1979–1985 under Minoru Kiyota), also learning from Noriaki Hakamaya and Kosai Fukushima. From ~1986, he served as professor at Nanzan University and director of the Nanzan Institute for Religion and Culture.

Paul Mendes-Flohr was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Brooklyn College and Brandeis University. He taught at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1972–2006) and the University of Chicago (~1999–2024).

Paul Mus was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and history/archaeology who studied under Jean Przyluski, Sylvain Lévi, and Paul Pelliot (~1923–1927). He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1937), Collège de France (1946–1970), and Yale University (~1950–1969).
Paul Nietupski is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at Columbia University (~1987–1993) and joined John Carroll University in ~1993.

Paul Pelliot was a scholar of Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Collège Stanislas, INALCO, Sciences Po, and under Émile Senart and Édouard Chavannes. He held posts at the EFEO, Collège de France (1909–1945), and the Institut de France.

Paul R. Katz is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He completed his doctorate at Princeton University (~1984–1990) and held a post at the Institute of Modern History, Academia Sinica, beginning around 2002.
Paul Regnaud was a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1870–1876) and served on the faculty at the University of Lyon (~1879–1908).
Paul Rouzer is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He held academic posts at Harvard University until ~2002 and subsequently at the University of Minnesota beginning in ~2002.

Paul Thieme was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Göttingen (~1923–1928). He held professorships and posts at the University of Breslau, University of Halle-Wittenberg, Goethe University Frankfurt, and the University of Tübingen (1960–1973).

Paul Tillich was a philosopher and religious studies scholar educated at Halle-Wittenberg, Breslau, Tübingen, and Berlin. He held posts at Berlin, Frankfurt, Union Theological Seminary (1933–1955), Harvard (~1955–1962), and Chicago (~1962–1965).

Paul W. Kroll is a Sinologist and linguist who studied at the University of Michigan (~1969–1976). He served at the University of Colorado Boulder as Associate Professor and department chair (~1989–2021).

Paul Williams is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Sussex and University of Oxford (Wadham College) and held posts at the University of Bristol (~1980–2011) and the University of Calgary (~1999).

Paula Kane Robinson Arai is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. She studied at Kalamazoo College and Harvard University (PhD ~1985–1993 under Masatoshi Nagatomi and Wilfred Cantwell Smith) and held posts at Vanderbilt and Louisiana State University.

Pe Maung Tin was a scholar of Buddhist studies, linguistics, and Indology. He studied at the University of Yangon and University of Calcutta, later serving as Professor of Pali at the University of Yangon (~1924–1946).
Pedro Manuel Castro Sánchez is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at the University of Sunderland, where he studied under Peter Harvey.

Pei-jung Wu is a scholar of art history, archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She earned a BA at National Taiwan University, studied under Shou-chien Shih, Yu-min Lee, and Hironobu Kohara, and completed her PhD under Donald F. McCallum at UCLA in 2002.
Peipei Qiu is a scholar in Japanology and Sinology. She studied at Peking University and Columbia University under Paul Rouzer, later taking up a post at Vassar College in ~1994.

Pema Bhum is a Tibetologist who previously taught Tibetan languages and letters at Lanzhou University and Indiana University (~1997–2002). He became Director of the Latse Contemporary Tibetan Cultural Library in ~2003.

Pema Chödrön is a Buddhist studies figure who attended Miss Porter's School and the UC Berkeley Graduate School of Education. She completed traditional training under Chögyam Trungpa (~1974–1987), Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche (~1994), and Sakyong Mipham.
